test_title: RRB NTPC CBT-I Official Paper (Held On: 4 Jan 2021 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: The difference between the simple interest and the compound interest on Rs.5000/- at 10% per annum for 3 years is:
solution:
**Given:**

Principal = Rs.5000

Rate of interest = 10% per annum 

Time = 3 years 

**Formulas used:**

Compound Interest = Amount - Principal 

⇒ Amount = P (1 + r/100)t

Simple Interest = Principal × Rate/100 × Time 

**Calculation:**

Compound Interest = 5000(1 + 10/100)³ - 5000 

⇒ 5000(110/100)³ - 5000 

⇒ 5000[11/10 × 11/10 × 11/10 - 1]

⇒ 5000[(1331 - 1000)/1000]

⇒ 5 × 331 = Rs.1655

Simple Interest = 5000 × 10/100 × 3 

⇒ Rs.1500 

Difference between compound interest & simple interest = Rs.1655 - Rs.1500

⇒ Rs.155

**∴ The required result = Rs.155**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Calculation of effective rate for compound interest:

Effective rate = x + x + x²/100 

Interest rate for 1 year = 10%

Effective rate for 2 years = 10 + 10 + (10 × 10)/100 = 10 + 10 + 1

⇒ 21%

Effective rate for 3 years = 21 + 10 + (21 × 10)/100 

⇒ 31 + 2.1 = 33.1% 

or 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/628068fbb6e7093e6c1c05c025e253b621ac2dd7efd040eeb7a81240f62d5ee3.png] 

Calculation of effective rate of interest for simple interest:

At 10% per annum for 3 years 

Rate = 10% × 3 = 30%

Difference between the CI and SI rate = 33.1% - 30% = 3.1%

**∴ Difference between the CI and SI for 3 years = 5000 × 3.1/100 **

**⇒ Rs.155**
